boundary: The first-order lane is a numerical cross-check of the certificate idealization, not physical validation. With a finite elastic stiffness the load-controlled limit coincides with the analytical rigid-plastic value for the canonical separation cases, and it remains a small conservative bias in the exactness case because the tangent operator loses positive definiteness before the ideal limit is reached; that bias is reported explicitly. The second-order and degrading lanes quantify the departure of a practical pushdown from the idealized limit and make no claim about real buildings.
engine_note: Elastic frame elements with an explicit element-internal end rotation and an elastic-perfectly-plastic rotational hinge in series at every member end; consistent P-Delta geometric stiffness; load-controlled increments with a plastic return mapping.
